claims.statement: convert-roms rewrites the library in place (new file next to the old one, old file deleted, romfiles row updated), while export-roms writes copies into a required -d/--directory and leaves both the originals and the database untouched, which is what makes lossy export targets safe.

ISO, GDI, WBFS, WUA and NUS exist only in export_roms' private format list, never in convert_roms::ALL_FORMATS; because config's PREFER_FORMAT choice list, the GraphQL PreferFormatValidator and the MCP tool all read ALL_FORMATS, those five can never become an auto-conversion target.

Since CHD work moved in-process, no format needs an external-tool probe: convert_roms::format_available is a pure string test over the nine built-in formats and a false is a soft stop returning Ok(()) (clap's PossibleValuesParser already rejects unknown --format values), while export_roms repeats the same inline table and bails with 'Not supported'.

format_supported_for_system restricts arcade systems to ARCADE_FORMATS = [ORIGINAL, ZIP]; convert_system turns a violation into a warning and early return, and the same function is reused by config::set_setting, the GraphQL set_prefer_format mutation and the MCP tool so a rejected format cannot be stored through a validated surface.

ConvertOpts { recompress, diff, check, prompt_for_parents } is the shared entry to conversion: convert-roms builds it from -r/-d/-c/-p, and import_roms::auto_convert calls convert_system with recompress:false, diff:false, check:true, prompt_for_parents:false, catching errors as 'Auto-conversion to {format} failed' so a failed conversion never rolls back a completed import.

convert-roms --save writes the destination format into the per-system PREFER_FORMAT with the raw config::set_string, bypassing the arcade validation the validated writers apply (though clap already confines the value to ALL_FORMATS); MCP's convert_roms tool instead reconstructs a convert-roms argv with only --system and --format, so MCP conversions never carry --recompress, --check or --save.
convert_system loads rom data with original_roms = true (only roms rows with original = true), while export_roms passes false and therefore also exports roms a DAT marks as non-original.

Compression settings are read per system (Some(system.id)) at conversion time: SEVENZIP_/ZIP_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM plus level keys and SEVENZIP_SOLID_COMPRESSION for archives, CHD_CD/DVD/HD/LD_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHMS, CHD_*_HUNK_SIZE and CHD_PARENTS for CHD, RVZ_COMPRESSION_ALGORITHM/LEVEL/BLOCK_SIZE (plus RVZ_SCRUB only in export_roms) for RVZ; CSO, ZSO, NSZ, WUX and ORIGINAL read none.

The solid flag is threaded through ToArchive and read from SEVENZIP_SOLID_COMPRESSION (ZIP hard-codes false), but the archive writer ignores it because entries are added one call at a time, with a TODO to batch a game's files into one solid block.

The minimum-chdman-version gates for Dreamcast CHDs and multi-track (split-bin) CDs are gone: with chd-rs linked in process nothing probes a chdman version, and multi-track CD CHDs are handled unconditionally by extract_cd's per-track '%t' naming.

Every conversion decodes the source into a neutral artefact (ISO, CUE/BIN set, NSP) written into a fresh create_tmp_directory under TMP_DIRECTORY, wrapped with the originating romfile in transcode::Decoded { source, inner }, so the caller can diff and delete the source afterwards.

Each game (each CHD, each archive) is converted inside its own SQL transaction that is committed only on the success path; a skip or check failure leaves the transaction uncommitted so romfiles/roms rows revert, while any file already written has to be deleted explicitly by the branch.

check_and_persist is the generic commit tail: on a Check error it prints 'Integrity check failed, reverting conversion', deletes the new file and returns false; otherwise it optionally prints the diff, then updates the romfile row and deletes the source - or, with rename_to_source set (the recompression paths), deletes the source first and renames the new file onto the old path.

Integrity checking a converted CHD, XSO or archive means extracting it into a tmp directory and hashing the extracted bytes against the DAT's expected hash and size; RVZ hashes the disc in place unless a DAT header exists. A failed conversion's output is deleted outright, never moved to Trash.

Persist::update rewrites romfiles.path and romfiles.size for the same row id, so a converted file keeps its identity and every roms.romfile_id stays valid; only when a multi-file game collapses into one archive or one CHD does the code create or reuse a single row and re-point each rom with update_rom_romfile before deleting the old rows.

print_diff normalizes both sides against the DAT rather than the old file: Before and After are printed as percentages of the summed expected rom.size, so converting an already-compressed source still reports both relative to the uncompressed original.

to_archive partitions the loaded games by extension in a fixed order (CHD, CSO, NSZ, RVZ, WUX, ZSO, archive, then leftovers), sorts CHD games so children convert before parents, skips a CHD that still has children, and leaves arcade CHDs (any rom with rom.disk) untouched.

Archive-to-archive conversion is a no-op when the source archive type already matches the target unless --recompress is set; with recompress the archive is rebuilt into the tmp directory and renamed over the original path. The pair of tests asserts the distinction through the file's mtime.

Parent CHDs are chosen by find_parent_chd: prompt_for_parents (-p) lists the system's parentless CHDs sorted by jaro-winkler similarity to the game name, otherwise the CHD_PARENTS boolean falls back to find_parent_chd_romfile_by_game, which takes the first game of the game's playlist and that game's CHD romfile; the link is persisted with update_romfile_parent after each successful conversion.

CHD-to-CHD recompression only rewrites children: the parent CHD is skipped by the 'CHD has children, skipping' guard, and the test asserts the parent's mtime is unchanged while the child's moves forward.

CUE/BIN to CHD is the branch that leaves two romfiles behind: the generated .cue is renamed next to the source and kept as its own row, while every BIN rom is re-pointed at the new CHD row; more than one archive or one CHD inside a single game is a hard bail.

to_xso, to_nsz and to_rvz accept only narrow source sets and drop everything else: XSO takes single-ISO archives, loose ISOs, DVD CHDs and the opposite XSO type (always via a decoded ISO), NSZ takes NSPs and single-NSP archives, RVZ takes ISOs and single-ISO archives; same-format recompression happens in place only under --recompress, and convert_roms always passes scrub = false, never reading RVZ_SCRUB.
A multi-track CD CHD is deliberately left alone when converting to CSO/ZSO because transcode::chd_to_iso returns None for any CHD that is not a DVD, which is what the *_should_do_nothing tests pin.

convert_roms::to_original takes only the check flag (recompress and diff never reach it, and no branch prints a diff); for arcade systems an extracted archive expands into a new directory named after the archive stem. Because CHD work is now a library call, a CHD failure propagates as an ordinary Err out of convert_system instead of breaking out of one loop.

export-roms opens no transaction and never calls Persist or Check: the destination directory is canonicalized and created up front, -o/--1g1r restricts the selection to games with sorting == Sorting::OneRegion, and every to_* function only writes files, so the database is read-only for the whole command, the WUA export's scan for update and DLC TMDs included.

export-roms copies rather than re-encodes sources that are already in the target format - ZIP to ZIP, 7z to 7z, CHD to CHD, CSO/ZSO either way, ISO to ISO and an existing GDI set with all its track files - with RVZ the exception: copied verbatim when RVZ_SCRUB is off, re-encoded through a temp ISO when it is on.

The export-only targets flatten rather than round-trip: to_iso keeps only the first track's 2048-byte user data (CD CHDs go CHD to CUE/BIN to ISO, HD/LD CHDs are skipped), to_wbfs writes a Wii WBFS from an ISO decoding RVZ through the tmp directory first, and to_gdi builds a GDI plus track files from CUE/BIN or copies an existing GDI set, skipping a CD CHD with no CUE alongside.

Conversion tests are one file per transition named test_<source>_to_<target>.rs and call the private to_* functions directly, passing recompress/diff/check and the CHD settings positionally; no-op transitions are asserted explicitly (*_should_do_nothing for convert, *_should_copy for export).

All CHD creation flows through src/chd.rs::create_chd, which packs the configured codec names into the header's four slots and calls chd_rs::create_cd/create_dvd/create_hd/create_ld inside run_blocking, so the synchronous crate runs on the blocking pool while the caller's progress bar becomes a byte bar; the CD progress denominator is chd_rs::cd_input_size and other types use the input file's length.

CHD extraction is symmetrical through src/chd.rs::extract_chd: the CHD is opened on the blocking pool with Chd::open or Chd::open_with_parent when a parent is known, then chd_rs::extract_cd handles CDs, chd_rs::extract_ld LaserDiscs and Chd::extract DVDs and hard disks.

chd-rs stages every output as `<output>.part` and renames it into place only on success, deleting the part file on failure — for write_part/Chd::extract, all of extract_cd's sheet and BINs, and extract_ld — so a failed CHD conversion or extraction leaves no partial file behind.

create_chd reproduces chdman's defaults rather than reinterpreting them: with no configured codec list it uses cdlz,cdzl,cdfl for CDs, avhu for LaserDiscs and lzma,zlib,huff,flac for DVDs and hard disks; a lone 'none' becomes four zero slots; and an unset hunk size takes the parent's, then 8 * CD_FRAME_SIZE for CDs and 4096 otherwise.

util::tool_version no longer exists: its last caller, ctrtool::get_version, went when CIA import moved to the in-process cia-rs crate, so no format shells out to an external binary. CHD reports the literal string 'built-in' as chd::get_version to info, the GraphQL dependencies query and the MCP status tool, and cia::get_version does the same.

CHD→CSO/ZSO is a deliberate no-op for multi-track CD CHDs on both paths because chd_to_iso returns None for any non-DVD CHD; the convert-roms and export-roms tests assert the absence of a destination file with no tool-version early return in front of them.

Multi-track CD CHD round trips are asserted unconditionally: convert to_original explodes a CD CHD into one romfiles row per track plus the .cue (three roms, three romfiles), and export to_original writes one BIN per track plus the CUE into the destination directory.

The playlist-driven CHD parent link is established on the forward ISO→CHD conversion, not only during recompression: find_parent_chd resolves via prompt_for_parent_romfile when prompting, otherwise via find_parent_chd_romfile_by_game when CHD_PARENTS is set, and the result is stored with update_romfile_parent.

export-roms' ORIGINAL path extracts each archive's entries into one temporary directory and renames each into `<destination>/<game>/<rom name>` for arcade systems (`<destination>/<rom name>` otherwise), so a merged set's `<clone>/` entries export under the ROM's own name.

convert-roms' to_wux converts loose WUDs and single-ROM archives whose ROM name ends in wud, and drops existing WUXs even under recompress because a WUX has no settings; to_archive turns a WUX into a WUD in the temp directory before archiving it.

export-roms' WUA, NUS and WUX targets accept WUDs, WUXs and single-WUD archives; the WUX target copies an existing WUX as it is, the WUA target bundles the library's newest update and DLC by title ID, and a NUS title exported as ORIGINAL is copied into a folder named after its game.
